correctness.rationale: Take s along the edge and V=n·x−C normal to it. An incoming radial displacement δ has (s,V)=(Aδ,Cδ), while an outgoing radial displacement δ′ has (1+(A+1)δ′,Cδ′). Solving V′=−κV and s′=ω−μV gives δ′=δ exp(−κt). At the on-cycle time the tangential matching condition is proportional to δ with shear coefficient C(1−E)/κ>0, so cancellation is exact and unique. On the reference edge the angular velocity is ωC/|x|²>0; both modes cross an adjoining ray in the same direction. Compactness over an edge, restricting the offset, and the simple section root with time derivative ω at δ=0 ensure the selected first crossing stays local. Even at a detuned finite shear the derivative of δ exp(−κt(δ)) at zero is E, so the period and transverse multiplier really are preserved. At tuning, the flight map transports each small incoming radial segment by an affine map with nonzero normal component at every intermediate time. These fixed-time lines are local coordinates, glue to the radial segments at crossings and synchronize under repeated revolutions (amplitude factor ∏E); distinct phases on the simple orbit cannot converge with zero relative time shift. Equal radii give A=−1/2 and the displayed coth formula. An independent exact-rational replay checks tuned and detuned ray identities on six unequal sectors with both signs of offset.
residual_risks: Only local isochrons and uniqueness for edgewise fixed flight time, not uniqueness among all possible phase properties or a global basin.

It identifies the precise parameter choice that removes finite-offset timing errors at every switch; this is appreciably stronger than calculating the linear response or verifying a regular polygon example.
